title: Headsprout Early Reading for Specific Literacy Difficulty: A Comparison Study
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether the computer-assisted reading program Headsprout Early Reading (HER) produces stronger literacy gains than the supplementary literacy support typically delivered by a school SENCO for children with specific literacy difficulty. The broader problem is the persistent attainment gap for struggling readers and the concern that many school-based interventions are eclectic, inconsistently delivered, and not strongly evidence-based.

The study compared HER, an internet-based, systematically sequenced phonics and early reading program, with treatment as usual (TAU), which consisted of SENCO-delivered instruction such as guided reading, paper-based phonics training, and word-recognition tasks. Participants were primary school children aged 6–9 in a Northern Irish school, all receiving free school meals and supplementary literacy support. Thirty-two pupils were analyzed after random assignment to HER or TAU.

Over approximately 7 months, children in the HER group completed 30-minute sessions five times per week in small groups using laptops and headphones, while the TAU group received daily 1:1 SENCO support. Outcomes were assessed with standardized measures of word/non-word recognition, sentence reading, and sight words, plus a teacher social-validity questionnaire. HER produced significantly greater gains than TAU on all reported reading outcomes, suggesting that systematic computer-assisted instruction can outperform the school’s usual eclectic literacy support. The paper also suggests HER may be more cost-effective and less staff-intensive, while noting that conventional SENCO instruction may not be sufficiently systematic to close the attainment gap.

identified_tools.name: Headsprout Early Reading
identified_tools.description: An internet-based computer-assisted early reading program that delivers systematic, individualized phonics and early literacy instruction with immediate feedback and mastery-based progression.
identified_tools.use_case: Compared against SENCO-delivered supplementary literacy instruction for primary school children with specific literacy difficulty over 7 months.

findings.finding_summary: Children receiving Headsprout Early Reading (HER) gained significantly more than the TAU group on word/non-word recognition over 7 months. Posttest mean scores were 99.41 (SD 7.13) for HER (n=17) versus 78.27 (SD 8.70) for TAU (n=15); the ANOVA reported F(1,30)=55.14, p=0.0001, with Cohen's d=2.65.
findings.measure: Phonics and Early Reading Assessment (PERA) word/non-word recognition

findings.finding_summary: HER produced significantly greater gains than TAU on sentence reading. Posttest mean scores were 97.53 (SD 8.64) for HER versus 88.67 (SD 9.85) for TAU; the ANOVA reported F(1,30)=14.44, p=0.002, with Cohen's d=0.96.
findings.measure: Phonics and Early Reading Assessment (PERA) sentence reading score (SRS)

findings.finding_summary: HER outperformed TAU on sight-word acquisition as measured by the Dolch words assessment. Posttest mean scores were 65.8 (SD 34.6) for HER versus 23.4 (SD 18.5) for TAU; the ANOVA reported F(1,30)=8.26, p=0.0001, with Cohen's d=1.53.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a randomized comparison study with pre/post measures and a concurrent control group, which supports relatively strong causal inference. However, the sample is small and from a single school, and the paper notes limited procedural-integrity documentation and some attrition.
impact_tier_rationale: All reported effects are large by the paper's own Cohen's d values (0.96 to 2.65), indicating strong impact on literacy outcomes. The gains are substantial on multiple reading measures, though generalizability is limited by the study context.
